title: User email lookups and writes are case-insensitive
detail: `user:find-for-auth`, `user:create` and `user:update` lowercase the email in their schema, `seedUser` and the signup guard lowercase it before lookup and insert, and `login` lowercases before the lookup and the unknown-email lockout count. Before, the blind index compared byte-exact, so `Max@Firma.de` failed to log in to `max@firma.de` and `user:create` could add a second account for the same address in other casing. Emails returned by these handlers are now always lowercase, and `user-data-rights:write:request-deletion-by-email` lowercases its input too. The admin boot seed (`seedAdminGuarded`, `seedBootstrapAdmin`, `ensureBootstrapAdminRoles`) still finds an account stored with upper case and rewrites its email to lower case. `runProdApp` and `runWorkerApp` lowercase every other stored email on each boot in the background through the executor (`normalizeStoredUserEmails` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/user`), so the event and the blind index follow.
migration: Nothing to do for accounts stored with upper case; the boot step repairs them. When the lowercase address already belongs to another live account, the boot step leaves both accounts unchanged and logs the count and the user ids as a warning ("user accounts whose lower-cased email belongs to another live account"); decide per pair which account stays and merge or delete the other one. Callers that compared a returned email against mixed-case input compare with `normalizeEmail` instead.

title: user-list: system-scope search; membership roles on tenants; emailVerified sort
user-list: roles multiSelect + tenants column; roles editable as SystemAdmin (fw#2384 follow-up)
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` and apply — migrates read_users.roles from text to jsonb USING roles::jsonb. Existing JSON array strings (`[]`, `["SystemAdmin"]`) convert cleanly. Consumers that wrote roles as a JSON-encoded string via user:create/update should pass string[] instead (parseRoles still accepts both on read).

title: user.locale no longer defaults to "de" (fw#1637).
detail: The entity-level default contradicted tenant-settings' own "en" default and silently overrode any app or tenant locale configuration for every new user. locale now stays unset until the client or a resolution chain provides one. Consumers that already fall back with `user.locale ?? "en"` are unaffected in shape but now see null instead of "de".
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` and apply — the migration emits `ALTER TABLE read_users ALTER COLUMN locale DROP DEFAULT`. Note that DROP DEFAULT only affects future inserts: existing rows keep the "de" the old default wrote, which no user ever chose. Your app therefore splits into pre-bump users on "de" and post-bump users on null, and each group resolves to a different language. Decide deliberately: either keep the old values (and state that pre-bump users stay German), or run `UPDATE read_users SET locale = NULL WHERE locale = 'de'` once so every user follows the same chain — the latter only if no UI ever let users edit the field, otherwise it erases real choices. If your app relied on the implicit German default, set an explicit fallback instead (fw#1653).

title: user.timezone field, wired into ctx.tz (fw#1636).
migration: Run `kumiko-schema generate` and apply — the migration adds `read_users.timezone`. No backfill: an unset timezone falls through to the tenant's, exactly as before the field existed.
